item.title: Alpha.15: storage format 2, a Windows installer and a daily channel
item.description: A new storage format that fixes two findings of the security review, so existing vaults must be recreated; Windows gets a setup program, a native window and automatic updates; and a signed daily build channel.

item.title: Alpha.14: a security review, its fixes, and everything merged since alpha.13
item.description: A code-level security review of the whole program, the fixes it asked for, a much faster sync, resumable moves to a stack of removable disks, and the twenty-odd features that had been waiting on the main branch since alpha.13.

item.title: Alpha.13: backups that nothing can change
item.description: Pick a folder on any device and Varsto keeps encrypted, read-only snapshots of it on your external storages, never on your devices, for as many days as you choose (90 by default). Restores go into a directory you name, from the app or the command line.

item.title: Alpha.12: small files in packs, and Varsto in Finnish and Swedish
item.description: Small encrypted blocks are now written in packs, so a folder of 20,000 small files becomes 79 objects on a bucket instead of 20,000. The interface, tray, menu bar, mobile shells and this website are available in Finnish and Swedish as well as English.

item.title: Alpha.9: data where you want it, repair by itself, signed updates, and every platform built in the open
item.description: Folders can be placed on chosen storages and moved between them, lost copies are repaired automatically, updates are signed with an offline key, peer-to-peer downloads fetch many blocks at once, and every package is now built, tested and photographed on GitHub's runners.

item.title: Alpha.8: a ledger that stays small, removable devices, and phones that keep nothing in clear text
item.description: The ledger now lists only what is new, keeps a cached view and prunes itself behind signed checkpoints; devices can be removed with new keys for everything written afterwards; phones keep encrypted folders as encrypted blocks; and the interface shows where your data is and how peer-to-peer traffic flows.

item.title: Alpha.7: pair devices with a code, Finder actions, and a real NAT path
item.description: Devices now pair from the interface with a one-time code, Finder can download a placeholder or free up space with a right-click, the macOS app installs from a disk image, devices reach each other through NAT, and removable disks can form a pool.

item.title: Alpha.6: the source is public, and every platform builds in the cloud
item.description: The repository is now public on GitHub under the PolyForm Shield licence, the native macOS and iOS apps build on GitHub Actions, Linux, Windows and Android build on short-lived cloud machines, and the interface was redone around a file view.

item.title: Alpha-0: the first vertical slice
item.description: A command-line tool that encrypts, stores and syncs a folder between two devices through storage you own, with a signed ledger you can check.
